title: Content-Type on multipart/form-data part without setting filename

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

According to section 4.4 of [RFC 7578](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7578#section-4.4), it is entirely correct to send a `Content-Type` header on any part, not only on parts representing files. However, neither `<input>` attributes nor `FormData` methods provide such option; a part is either (implicitly) `text/plain`, or it will have a filename.

A capable server could use the 'Content-Type' part header to interpret the field content slightly differently, using the same endpoint and the same multipart handler code (e.g., a part with the name `message` is still a message, regardless of how it was encoded).

Here are some use cases:
 - Content reporting route:
   - `{ 'description': '<problem description>', 'page': '<page id>', 'debug-info': { … } }` with `Content-Type: application/json` from web app
   - The same structure, but XML/CBOR/Protobuf/etc. encoded with appropriate Content-Type from native app
   - `<problem description>` with `text/plain` from lightweight JS-less version that can't fill in other fields
 - Rich text support:
   - `text/markdown` (or any other structured format, like `text/html`) from web-based editor
   - `text/plain` (or simply no Content-Type) in case when such editor could not be loaded; set to avoid misinterpretations and unnecessary parsing
 - Examples above, but in a form that also contains a file part
 - (obscure one) `text/plain;charset: …`  would allow sending fewer bytes for some languages

### What solutions exist today?

From the client side (if server modification is not possible), there is only one option: manually construct the request body, which is error-prone — or delegate this task to an existing, well-tested library.

From the server side:
 - Use different routes or field names for different content types
   - Easy to implement
   - Requires different multipart fields (or routes) on different clients
   - Looks unnatural
 - Guess content type from content
   - Guessing isn't always possible
 - Ignore filename field
   - Some frameworks handle 'files' and 'non-files' differently, based on this field

### How would you solve it?

### For HTML `<input>`

Introduce a new attribute `mime` (or `content-type`, or even `enctype`), which would set the `Content-Type` header of the corresponding part when present (if `enctype` of corresponding `<form>` is `multipart/form-data`, of course). Since no such attribute currently exists (at least, for `<input>`), this change would not break existing code.

### For JS `FormData`

Possible changes that shouldn't break any existing JS code:
 - `.append(name, string, type)`
   - Easy to read
   - Only supports text data
   - Confusing: `.append(name, file|blob, filename)` already exists
 - `.append(name, string|file|blob, { noFilename: true })`
   - Explicitly indicates that the `filename` field should be omitted
   - As above, this overlaps with the existing 3-argument `append`
 - `isNotFile` boolean field in the second argument of `Blob(blobParts, options)`
   - Not a change to `FormData` directly, but to `Blob`

### Anything else?

_No response_
